title: Cheating, lying and stealing
intro: Lying is the key to every evil – and the truth can free us from bad habits.

learn.html: Good qualities that make our behaviour beautiful are the goal of upbringing and education, while bad qualities give a bad picture of us. Among the bad qualities, lying stands out – it is the beginning of many other bad deeds and qualities.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah tells us that only those who do not believe in Allah’s signs dare to invent lies – and they are the real liars. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nahl 16:105)</small>
A lie is an untruth said on purpose. If these two things come together, a person has a dangerous and serious illness of the soul:

items: lying often when talking to other people
feeling no guilt at all for the lie they told

learn.html: Lying is a quality of hypocrites, so it must not be found in Muslims. The Prophet (SAW) was asked whether a believer can be a coward, and he said he can. “Can a believer be a miser?” – “He can,” he answered. “And can a believer be a liar?” – “No,” he said.
People have weaknesses, so in their behaviour they may have some qualities that do not suit a believer. But a believer must not be a liar.

learn.title: Rare exceptions
learn.html: In exceptional situations, when the community or a person’s life is at stake, saying an untruth is allowed: in times of war, and to make peace between two Muslims.

Lying leads to other bad deeds, like cheating and stealing. Cheating is deceiving another person on purpose and trying to hide the true facts. Stealing is taking another person’s property, of any value.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Lying is the key to every evil: whoever lies also steals, and whoever steals also does other major sins.

Cheating and stealing harm another person’s reputation, dignity and property. So for these sins a person must, in this world, ask halal – forgiveness – from the one who was harmed. If something material was damaged, it is a duty to pay it back.

In Islam, stealing has a punishment in this world and in the next. Today, when stealing is very widespread, the only way to root out this dangerous illness is a firm belief that it is a major sin that brings consequences.

learn.text: A story from the time of the Prophet (SAW)

learn.html: A man came to the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I have many bad habits. Which one should I leave first?” The Prophet said: “First leave lying, and always tell the truth.” The man promised to do so and went home.

When night fell, he got ready to go and steal. But before he left the house, he remembered the promise he had given the Prophet: “If the Prophet asks me tomorrow where I was, what will I say? Will I say I went stealing? No, I can’t. But I can’t lie either. If I tell the truth, everyone will hate me and call me a thief, and I will be punished for stealing.” So that night he decided not to steal – and he left this bad habit.

The next day he wanted to drink wine, but as he was about to do it, he thought: “What will I tell the Prophet if he asks what I did today? I can’t lie, and if I tell the truth, people will hate me, because a Muslim is not allowed to drink wine.” And so he gave up the idea of drinking wine.
And so, whenever this man felt like doing something bad, he remembered his promise to always tell the truth. In this way he left his bad habits one by one.

practice.title: What does it mean?
pairs: Deceiving someone and hiding the true facts
Asking forgiveness from the one you harmed

practice.title: When is an untruth allowed?
practice.prompt: Tap the exceptions the book gives, then tap Check.

options.text: To make peace between two Muslims
To get out of maktab by saying you were sick
options.why: That is an ordinary lie – a believer must not be a liar.

options.text: To copy answers in a test
options.why: Copying in a test is cheating.

options.text: To blame your brother or sister
options.why: Blaming someone else is a lie that hurts them.

practice.title: The man who left his bad habits
items: He asks the Prophet (SAW) which bad habit to leave first
The Prophet says: “First leave lying, and always tell the truth.”
At night he wants to steal, but remembers his promise
The next day he wants to drink wine, but remembers again
He leaves his bad habits one by one

questions.q: Why is lying called “the key to every evil”?
options: Whoever lies also steals, and whoever steals does other major sins
Because it is a small thing

questions.q: According to the hadith, can a believer be a liar?
What must you do if you damaged someone’s things?
options: Ask them to forgive you and pay it back

questions.q: Which two signs together show a serious illness of the soul?
options: Lying often and feeling no guilt

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 What is a lie, and which sins does it lead to? In which situations may a person say an untruth?
✏️ Task: Read the story from the time of the Prophet (SAW) and write questions about it in your maktab notebook. Swap questions with the friend next to you and answer each other’s.
💭 Explain what truth means to you, and what cheating, lying and stealing mean. How often do you think about the results of your deeds?

📋 Draw a table with the columns Always / Often / Sometimes / Never and put an X: I say I was sick when I don’t come to maktab · I don’t tell my parents or family the whole truth · I tease my brother or sister because I want things to go better for me · I say bad words or swear when I get angry · I tell a secret even when someone asks me to keep quiet · I copy in a test at school if I can · I’m good at copying when there is a test in maktab. Compare with a friend in maktab.
